champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency
ordered_diagnoses: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin laxity with coalesced papules and loss of elasticity, primarily affecting flexural areas
salient_findings: Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas
Severe skin sagging with loss of elasticity
Thick and leathery skinfolds on the neck, axillae, inguinal regions, abdomen, and limbs
key_facts: Younger sister has the same skin symptoms
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%)
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis
Compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene

raw.champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency
raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin laxity, yellowish papules, and excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments, combined with low clotting activity of factor X and prolonged prothrombin time, are consistent with this diagnosis. The compound heterozygous sequence variation in the GGCX gene further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum
rejected.why: While the patient's skin symptoms are similar to those of pseudoxanthoma elasticum, the presence of multiple coagulation factor deficiency and the specific genetic mutation suggest a more complex disorder.

rejected.label: Cutis laxa
rejected.why: Cutis laxa is characterized by loose, hanging skin, but it does not typically involve the calcification of elastic fibers or coagulation factor deficiencies seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Elastosis perforans serpiginosa
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by perforating elastic fibers, but it does not typically involve the widespread skin laxity or coagulation factor deficiencies seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Anetoderma
rejected.why: Anetoderma is characterized by localized areas of skin atrophy, but it does not typically involve the systemic symptoms or genetic mutations seen in this patient.
